approach: Root cause: docs/decisions.md is prose and nothing links a decision to the code or limit it governs, so a change that reverses a decision (D08, job 20261010-225741-yvk0) or a stated limit (drain help "at most 8", job 20261105-180339-w5h7) is found only at the final verdict. Fix in four parts. (1) A small athena-data module `decision_links` defines the `[[governs]]` table (decision id plus paths: an exact file, or a directory prefix ending `/`), the constant `GATE_REASON_PREFIX`, and one pure function `unreconciled(base_links, cand_links, base_log, cand_log, changed_paths)`. It returns each governed decision whose paths the change touches, unless the candidate adds a `[[link]]` with `older = <id>` whose `newer` heading is new in the candidate's decisions.md. Any link status (amended or superseded) reconciles, so a non-reversing edit has a cheap route: a one-line "checked, unchanged" entry plus an `amended` link. (2) `Athena::check_and_verify` (run/mod.rs) calls `Athena::unreconciled_decisions` (run/checks.rs) first, before the CI push, the early pull request, the checks and the verifier. On a hit the job closes failed with a reason that starts with `GATE_REASON_PREFIX` and names each decision id, its governed paths and the fix. (3) NEW this round, answering the critic's major finding: `retry_findings` (reading.rs) today returns None for a job with no verification record, so a job closed by this gate would hand the producer nothing. It now also returns the closing reason of a job that closed Failed with that prefix and has no verification. `athena retry` then lists the decision ids in the producer brief's "Findings you must address" block (briefs.rs `must_address_block`, existing, unchanged). (4) `ConfirmedLinks` (athena-cli decisions.rs) reads and validates `[[governs]]` through the same athena-data parser; backtest.rs reports a governed id absent from the log as a condition (a) finding. D08 is mapped to crates/athena-git/src/snapshot.rs and crates/athena-core/src/run/candidate.rs. For the limit class, the drain help text becomes a template with a `{ceiling}` placeholder filled from `athena_data::config::MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING` by `drain_after_help(ceiling)`, attached in a new `cli_command()` that `main` uses.

decisions.choice: Get the finding to the producer by extending `retry_findings` (reading.rs, line 1780) to return the closing reason of a job that closed Failed with `GATE_REASON_PREFIX` and has no verification. The gate stays in `check_and_verify`.
decisions.reason: The critic's finding is right: `retry_findings` returns None unless `records.jobs[id].verification` exists (reading.rs 1788-1794), and the gate closes the job before `verification_stage`, so no record exists and the retry brief (mod.rs 923-927, briefs.rs 463-467) would carry nothing. Extending the one function that builds the retry findings is the smallest fix: no verifier cost, the mark is spent so the retry starts from the base, and the existing `must_address_block` shows the text. It is one function plus its inline tests, in the file that already holds the neighbouring retry tests (5875-5972).

rejected.option: (a) Send the finding back inside `producer_loop` (producer.rs 156-343), like `loop_replay`
rejected.why: It would give the producer the finding in the same run, but it needs edits in producer.rs and send_back.rs (the send-back text only knows unmet and unchanged files) and a test of the work tree before a commit exists. producer.rs is on the brief's out-of-scope list. The pure function takes plain texts, so a later send-back can reuse it. Named here as the follow-up; the user is asked in open_questions.

rejected.option: (c) Make the gate a failing CheckRun so the verifier's finding carries it
rejected.why: verification_stage always starts the verifier (verification.rs comment at line 174: the verifier always runs), which spends model cost on a candidate already known to fail. It is also unclear a failed check yields a blocking finding that `retry_findings` reads.

decisions.choice: The reconcile signal is a new `[[link]]` in docs/decision-links.toml (older = governed id, newer = a heading new in the candidate's decisions.md), not a scan of prose for 'Amended by'.

The check stays a pure comparison of two toml texts and two heading lists. The link's status is not read, so both `amended` and `superseded` reconcile.

steps: Create crates/athena-data/src/decision_links.rs and register it in athena-data lib.rs. Define `Governs` (serde, Clone, PartialEq, Eq, Debug); `pub const GATE_REASON_PREFIX` (a plain sentence start such as `decisions not reconciled:`, with none of the words ENVIRONMENT_PREFIX uses); `parse_governs(text) -> Result<Vec<Governs>, String>` (id shape `D` plus 2 or more digits, non-empty paths, no leading `/` or `..`); `link_pairs(text)` reading only `older` and `newer` of each `[[link]]`; `Governs::covers(path)` (exact, or directory prefix when the entry ends `/`); and `unreconciled(base_links, cand_links, base_log, cand_log, changed) -> Result<Vec<Unreconciled>, String>`. A decision is reconciled when the candidate has a pair (id, N) the base lacks, where `## N ` starts a line in the candidate log and in no line of the base log; the link's status is not read. The base's `[[governs]]` judges; a candidate list that does not parse counts as no new links. Inline unit tests for D08, D12 and D02: not touched, touched without a link, touched with a link, a link for another id, a link whose heading is not new, an `amended` link, a directory prefix versus a sibling path, a deleted path, a renamed path, a malformed list.

demonstrations.observes: Pure: `unreconciled` driven with literal toml and log strings. For each of D08, D12 and D02: a change touching a governed path with no new link is returned naming the id; the same change with a new `[[link]]` plus a new heading returns nothing; also covered: a link whose newer heading is not new, a link for another id, a directory prefix versus a sibling path, a deleted path, a renamed path (delete plus add), an `amended` link, and a malformed candidate list. End-to-end (`governed_edit_closes_before_the_verifier_starts`): the repo commits docs/decision-links.toml with `[[governs]]` for D02 (README.md) and D12 (src/), and docs/decisions.md with matching headings; the fake producer edits README.md only; the job closes Failed, the reason starts with `GATE_REASON_PREFIX`, names D02 and README.md, `!is_environment_reason`, and the verifier counter is 0. `governed_edit_with_an_amending_entry_and_link_reaches_the_verifier`: the producer also appends a D03 entry to decisions.md and a `[[link]]` older D02 newer D03; the verifier is called once and the reason lacks the gate text.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the call in `check_and_verify` removed, or `unreconciled` returning empty, the governed-edit job is not closed Failed naming D02 and the verifier counter is not 0; the pure tests for D08, D12 and D02 each fail.
demonstrations.seam: Production entry points: `athena_data::decision_links::unreconciled` (pure, literal strings, no double; added by step 1) and `Athena::go` -> `produce_and_verify` -> `check_and_verify` -> `unreconciled_decisions` (added by steps 6 and 7). Fixture: existing `athena_with`, `repo_with_config`, `commit_file`, `base_script`, `counting`, `finished_job` in run/tests.rs (all exist; fixtures read at lines 187, 219, 295, 341, 2152). The wrapper script that sets the producer's edits and counts verifier calls is added by step 8; the check logic lives in athena-data and run/checks.rs, never in the script.

demonstrations.method: Unit tests in main.rs over the real command and the template function.
demonstrations.observes: Test one renders the long help of `drain` from `cli_command()` and asserts it contains `format!("at most {}", athena_data::config::MAX_CONCURRENCY_CEILING)`. Test two calls `drain_after_help(13)` and asserts it contains `at most 13` and not `at most 8`, simulating a changed constant. A third assertion shows the `{ceiling}` placeholder never survives.
demonstrations.fails_without: With the literal `at most 8` kept in the text, the `drain_after_help(13)` assertion fails, and the rendered-help test fails as soon as the constant differs from 8.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `drain_after_help(ceiling: u32) -> String` and `cli_command() -> clap::Command` in crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, added by step 5. The ceiling is the function argument; the constant is read only inside `cli_command()`. The `Cli::command()` plus long-help render pattern in the existing main.rs tests exists and is reused.

demonstrations.method: Search plus two end-to-end tests: the gate closes before the verifier, and the producer of the retry receives the decision ids.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core run::tests::produce_and_verify_order_tests::governed_edit_closes_before_the_verifier_starts && cargo test -p athena-core run::tests::produce_and_verify_order_tests::a_retry_of_a_gated_job_briefs_the_producer_with_the_decision_ids && cargo test -p athena-core reading::tests::retry_findings_carry_the_reason_of_a_job_closed_by_the_decision_gate
demonstrations.observes: Grep `unreconciled_decisions` in crates/athena-core/src/run/mod.rs: the call sits in `check_and_verify` before `push_ci_branch`, the early pull request and `verification_stage`. Test 1 drives `Athena::go`, observes the `failed` UI line and `finished.reason` naming D02 and the paths, and a verifier count of 0. Test 2 then asks `try again on <first>` with `athena.ask` and runs `go`; a wrapper over `counting` records each producer `spec.user_prompt`; the second job's brief must contain `## Findings you must address`, `D02`, and `README.md`. Test 3 (reading.rs, inline, records built by the existing `records_with`) asserts `retry_findings` returns the redacted reason for a Failed job with the prefix and no verification, returns None for the same reason without the prefix, and is unchanged for a job with a verification (existing assertions at 5889 and 5969 still hold). A resume at the verifier stage (`recorded_checks` Some) and a nested run skip the call, shown by `governed_check_is_skipped_for_a_resume_at_the_verifier`.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the `retry_findings` change the second job's brief has no `## Findings you must address` block and no D02 (today `retry_findings` returns None when the job has no verification), so tests 2 and 3 fail; a call placed after `verification_stage`, or no call, leaves the verifier called at least once, which test 1 asserts is 0.
demonstrations.seam: Entry points `Athena::go` (via `athena_with`, exists) and `reading::retry_findings` (exists, changed by step 7). Fixture: `counting` plus a prompt-capturing wrapper (added by step 8) injected as the `Script` argument of `athena_with`; the brief text is built by the real `producer_brief_with_evidence`, never by the double. The resume case reuses the existing resume-mark fixture in run/tests.rs, extended in step 8.

demonstrations.method: Run the three checks Athena runs on the result, over the whole workspace.
demonstrations.command: cargo fmt --all --check && cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings && cargo test --locked
demonstrations.observes: All three exit 0. The test run includes the decisions.md pin test, the backtest condition (a) equality `hits.len() == links.len()` on the real log and list, tests/drain.rs `drain_help_documents_the_flags_and_lists_every_stop_reason`, the retry tests in reading.rs, and every existing run/tests.rs job test (their repositories have no docs/decision-links.toml, so `show_file` gives None and the step does nothing).
demonstrations.fails_without: fmt fails on any unformatted new file; clippy `-D warnings` fails on an unused function if the check is not wired in; test fails if D156 edits earlier bytes of decisions.md, if D156 holds a phrase the backtest parses and has no link, if the help text lost a stop-reason label, or if the governed tests run against a missing check.
demonstrations.seam: The entry points are the three cargo commands, run by the verifier in the producer's tree with the repository's own docs, tests and `Cargo.lock`; no double. The seam exists today (the commands listed under 'Checks Athena will run').

demonstrations.method: A test that the check refuses only governed-path changes, pure tests of the matching rule, and the unchanged refusal-corpus replay.
demonstrations.command: cargo test -p athena-core run::tests::produce_and_verify_order_tests::ungoverned && cargo test -p athena-data decision_links && cargo test -p athena-core --test refusal_corpus
demonstrations.observes: `ungoverned_edit_reaches_the_verifier`: a job whose producer edits README.md in a repo whose list governs only src/ closes on the normal path with the verifier called once. Pure tests show a delete and a rename of a governed path are refused, while a sibling path (`src/a.rs` vs governed `src/a/`) and a bare directory prefix are not. No reading rule changes: the refusal corpus (`corpus_cases_get_the_expected_outcome`, `corpus_covers_the_listed_input_forms`) is the reading gate and is untouched, so the replay of accepted readings stays at 0 newly refused. The extra refusals are changes to governed paths only; measured volume: 8 matching lines of 200 recent commits in HISTORY.txt touch the two D08 files.
demonstrations.fails_without: A check that refused every change, or matched by substring, would close the ungoverned job Failed, and the prefix-sibling pure test would fail.
demonstrations.seam: Same `athena_with`/`commit_file`/counting script as criterion 3 (exist) and `unreconciled` with literal strings (added by step 1). The corpus test runs as it is; I read its two test names, not a result.
